name: marcella gnocchi sauce
instructions:
Marcella Hazan's famous three-ingredient tomato sauce, kept in the cookbook as THE GNOCCHI SAUCE — she recommends the basic tomato/onion/butter sauce be used on GNOCCHI in particular, and it's very simple, requiring no blender. From Essentials of Classic Italian Cooking.

(The rest of the tomato pasta sauce family — sicilian pesto rosso, vodka sauce, pasta piperade, marcella eggplant sauce — is RETIRED to retired/; see notes.)

=== INGREDIENTS ===

- 28-oz can whole peeled tomatoes (San Marzano ideal — canned whole, not diced, not paste)
- 1 medium yellow onion, peeled and halved (NOT chopped — kept in halves)
- 5 tablespoons unsalted butter
- salt to taste
- gnocchi (Marcella's recommended pairing — the reason this recipe survives; short pasta shapes also fine)

=== PROCEDURE ===

1. Combine tomatoes, butter, onion halves, and a pinch of salt in a saucepan.
2. Simmer uncovered on low for ~45 minutes, stirring occasionally and crushing the tomatoes with the back of a spoon as they soften.
3. Fish out and discard the onion halves before serving (they've done their aromatic job).
4. Toss with cooked gnocchi (or short pasta).
notes:
Marcella Hazan's 3-ingredient tomato sauce (Essentials of Classic Italian Cooking). Split out from the former italian-tomato-sauces.json (Variant A) into its own file, and RENAMED 'MARCELLA GNOCCHI SAUCE' (September 2026): she recommends this basic tomato/onion/butter sauce for GNOCCHI in particular, and it's very simple — no blender required. That's the niche that kept it on the menu when the rest of the tomato-sauce family retired.

=== THE REST OF THE FAMILY IS RETIRED ===

Sicilian pesto rosso, vodka sauce, pasta piperade, and marcella eggplant sauce were moved to retired/ (September 2026): they just never make it onto the menu — the amount of effort required for very little nutrition, and awkward leftovers. This sauce survives on the opposite math: minimal effort, no blender, and a specific job (gnocchi).

=== WHY IT WORKS WITH ONLY THREE INGREDIENTS ===

Hazan's insight is that a whole peeled canned tomato + butter + onion, given enough time (~45 min uncovered), builds a sauce that reads more complex than the ingredient list suggests. Butter adds richness and rounds acidity in a way olive oil can't at this simplicity. The onion halves perfume the sauce without becoming a chunky component — that's why they go in whole and come out before serving. No garlic, no basil, no oregano, no chili — the restraint is the recipe.

=== DON'T CHOP THE ONION ===

The onion halves are meant to be discarded. Chopping the onion turns it into part of the sauce texture and changes the dish.

=== UNSALTED BUTTER, GENEROUS ===

Hazan calls for 5 tablespoons per 28-oz can. Don't cut it — the butter is doing structural work, not just flavor. Unsalted so you control the seasoning.

=== SAN MARZANO IF POSSIBLE ===

Whole peeled San Marzano tomatoes are what the recipe was tuned to. Other whole peeled canned tomatoes work; diced canned tomatoes read watery here.

=== FORMER SIBLINGS (ALL IN retired/) ===

- sicilian-pesto-rosso: raw blended sun-dried-tomato + almond pesto.
- vodka-sauce: tomato paste + cream cross-family outlier.
- pasta-piperade: blended vegetable-tomato base.
- marcella-eggplant-sauce: fried eggplant folded into a garlic-tomato base. Also Marcella.

=== DIFFERENTIATION FROM THE RAGU FAMILY ===

This recipe and its siblings tagged 'tomato pasta sauce' are deliberately narrow — protein-free tomato sauces, whole-or-blended (never knife-diced into discrete chunks). For protein-forward, long-simmered, cutting-board-cut counterparts, see the ragu family: [[bolognese]], [[spaghetti-and-meatballs]].
